title: feat(tools): SK50 holders and ER50 collet chucks on the 40 and 50 tapers
body:
Stacked on #4251 (which stacks on #4240). This PR contains the commits of both. Merge #4240, then #4251, then this PR after `git merge origin/main` and a new gate. Do not merge this PR before them.

## What changed

Third slice of #3919. The built-in holder library gets:

- **SK50** (DIN 69871 / DIN ISO 7388-1 size 50): Ø69.85 gauge, Ø97.5 flange, 3.2 standoff, 15.9 flange. It has ER16-ER50 collet chucks and every Weldon bore (6-20 mm, 1/4-3/4 in). The default gauge length is 100. It is in `crates/tools/src/holder_library_din.rs`, after SK40.
- **ER50** (Ø5-34 collets, Ø78 M64×2 nut, drawn 40 long) in the one ER table. It is on BT40, CAT40, SK40, BT50, CAT50 and SK50, with a default gauge length of 100. There is no standalone ER50 chuck.
- **SK50 is a spindle mount**: `SPINDLE_MOUNTS` has 14 names, with SK50 after SK40. The app test `every_library_taper_is_a_spindle_mount` keeps the list equal to the library.

The ER50 nut is wider than a 40-taper flange. The body is drawn at the nut width up to the flange front, with no flare. The flange steps in from it, so the outline is never smaller than the steel.

Each number and its source is in `docs/decisions/3919-standard-holders-3.md`.

Left out, with the reasons in the decision file:
- SK50 shrink-fit: the slice-2 shrink-fit tables have no SK50 table.
- TG75 / TG100: TG is a trade system, and we found no standard table.
- Morse MT2-MT5: DIN 228 fixes only the taper. The collar below the spindle face has no standard table.
- NMTB 30 / 40: we found no published flange table.
- Hydraulic and milling chucks: each maker designs its own body.
- A standalone ER50 chuck.
- SF32: it waits for the owner's measurements.

## Pinning tests

- `holder_library::din::sk50_tests::*` (new file `crates/tools/src/holder_library_sk50_tests.rs`):
  - `sk50_and_er50_match_the_recorded_table`
  - `the_sk50_and_er50_entries_are_listed`
  - `the_sk50_er50_outline_is_the_table`
  - `a_bt40_er50_body_wider_than_its_flange_is_drawn_whole`
  - `an_er50_chuck_takes_its_collet_range`
- These tests are updated for the new rows: `the_tapers_and_nuts_match_the_recorded_table`, `the_din_entries_are_listed`, `the_50_taper_entries_are_listed`, `the_shrink_entries_are_listed` (SK50 has no shrink-fit entry), `the_picker_shows_one_weldon_row_for_each_taper` and `the_new_library_tapers_are_spindle_mounts` (post).

## Gate results (head 5ea83cb93, base #4251 head 9921f2961)

winbuild (Windows, 5 jobs):
- `cargo test -p camcraft-tools --lib`: pass, 219 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --lib`: pass, 161 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass, no warnings.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test holder_library --test machine_default_holder --test holder_reference`: pass, 12 + 7 + 14 passed, 0 failed.

Not exercised: the light lane and the heavy lanes. No toolpath and no post output changed, so the example catalog suites do not apply. The UI was not started.

title: feat(pathkernel): an Outside piece starts at the stock edge with a proved approach from the air
body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

Writer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/4254#issuecomment-7207515978 (worker K4c-air-approach).

## What changed

A stay-down link can now end with an approach from the air. The approach is a straight stretch from the nearest place of the air to the start of an open piece on a stock edge loop. The link stage proves it. The plan has no new step kind, and the transition table of `Plan::new` does not change.

- `crates/pathkernel/src/link/approach.rs` (new): the approach proof and the fourth try of the link (`from_air`).
- `crates/pathkernel/src/link/proof.rs`: the chord proof is split into its room test, its crossing test and its swath test. The three tries of K4 are now one function (`tries`), so that the way out to the air uses them.
- `crates/pathkernel/src/link/route.rs`: `project` is visible to the link module.
- The order stage does not change (decision 4 in the record).

## The rule

The next cut must be an open piece whose start is on a stock edge loop. The approach starts at the place of an air loop nearest to that start, within a tool radius. The approach holds only when all of these are true:

- Each sample is in the air or the edge band, out of the part zone, more than a tool radius from each keep-out area, and not inside the cutter-centre area.
- The stretch holds in the legal room of the entry stage.
- The stretch crosses no cut made and no link, and touches no planned cut away from the ends of the link.
- The disc swept along the stretch, less the swath of the next piece, lies within a tool radius of the air. The air starts one tool radius outside the stock, so that rest is outside the stock.

Thus each piece of stock that the approach cuts is also cut by the next piece. The test is exact polygon geometry. Its only tolerance is the polygon flattening (`AREA_TOL`, 2 x `ROOM_TOL` = 10 um). No strip of uncut stock is open by a constant.

A piece whose start is not on a stock edge keeps the present rule. Where no proof holds, the link lifts with the reason of the straight link.

## Pins

Negative pins first (`crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/air_approach.rs`, in the `laws` directory suite):

- `an_approach_that_would_cut_stock_off_the_curve_is_refused`: a tooth of stock beside the start. A mutation run without the area test makes this pin fail.
- `an_approach_near_a_keep_out_at_the_stock_edge_is_refused`
- `an_approach_beside_a_part_that_reaches_out_of_the_stock_is_refused`
- `a_piece_that_does_not_start_at_the_stock_edge_keeps_its_lift_and_its_reason`

Positive pins:

- `a_link_comes_in_from_the_air_to_a_piece_at_the_stock_edge`
- `each_approach_of_the_bands_cuts_only_the_swath_of_its_piece`: each approach of the disc band and the dog-bone band is checked against the stock box of the case, not against the kernel's air.

Pins measured again, with no constant tuned:

- `order_link::k4_link_rule_holds_and_each_lift_is_named`
- `k4_order_link::kernel_order_and_link_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone` (it now also prints the places of the full-width feeds)
- `k3_load::kernel_load_control_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone` (merged in PR #4265; it reads the same Outside plans)
- `link_rule::a_link_leaves_a_cut_at_the_stock_edge_runs_in_the_air_and_comes_back_over_cleared_stock`: its first assertion pinned the old refusal. That link now stays as an approach.

## Readings

| Fixture (Auto / Inside / Outside) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| disc pocket (law suite) | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| disc band (law suite) | 13 / 0 / 13 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| dog-bone band (law suite) | 15 / 0 / 15 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| pocket with an island (law suite) | 7 / 7 / 5 | 7 / 7 / 5 |

| Motion pin | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| disc, Inside | 0 lifts, 0 crossings | 0 lifts, 0 crossings |
| disc, Outside | 13 lifts, 0 crossings; over 402, worst 145, full 0 | 0 lifts, 0 crossings; over 415, worst 145, full 0 |
| dog bone, Inside | 0 lifts, 0 crossings | 0 lifts, 0 crossings |
| dog bone, Outside | 15 lifts, 0 crossings; over 724, worst 167, full 0 | 0 lifts, 0 crossings; over 739, worst 180, full 1 |

The record's target of 0 lifts on the disc is met. No lift stays on the disc.

On the dog bone one approach arrives at full width, at (-2.40, 25.00) on the top stock edge. The material is in the swath of the next piece. Thus it is not a gouge and not stock off the curve. But no stage reads that load yet, because the load stage reads the cuts and not the links. Follow-up: #4272.

The K3 rows (moves above the limit, worst degrees, unnamed moves) change on Outside only. Disc: none 402/145/13 to 415/145/19; constant 334/118/74 to 344/122/81. Dog bone: none 724/167/3 to 739/180/13; constant 678/143/66 to 683/143/69. The decision record has the table.

## Decision

`docs/decisions/4254-kernel-air-approach.md`. Summary:

- The approach is the last stretch of a proved stay link. It is not a lift-free re-entry step.
- The proof uses the area of the swept disc.
- The way to the air uses the three tries of K4.
- The order stage needs no new rule, because the direction fixes the start of an open piece and the walk already asks the link stage for a proved path.

Dropped: a new plan step, a tangent approach, an arc lead.

## Gate (final head)

- `cargo check --tests -p camcraft-pathkernel`, then `-p camcraft-motion`: ok.
- `camcraft-pathkernel` `laws`: 140 passed.
- `camcraft-motion` `kernel_laws`: 30 passed.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` on both crates: ok.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel`: 4 steps ok (pathkernel build, lib, laws; motion kernel_laws).
- `cargo xtask gate light --base origin/side/path-kernel`: 7 steps ok.
- The branch merges `origin/side/path-kernel` at df9ec30b6 (PR #4265) without a conflict.

## Not exercised

- No planner calls the link stage yet. Thus the output of the old planners is identical. The example catalog suites were not run, because no post and no planner toolpath changes.
- The engagement of the approach is not controlled (#4272).
- Stock edges that are not straight were tested only with the tooth fixture. Inch units and work planes other than XY were not tested.
- The test file `air_approach.rs` joins the `laws` directory suite. No new top-level test binary.

It checks the power by name (more than 0, at most 100 % of the source's maximum), converts to `WaterjetParams` with `Voice::LASER`, and runs the same planner, tabs, emitter, kerf law and cover law. A note states the requested power. No CL record carries the power yet (slice 3, the laser post).

- **"My library" source** in the tools list (`tool_library_dialog/components.rs`):

  - "Show compatible parts" shows only the parts that fit the picked part (`compatible_parents` and `compatible_children`).
  - The buttons act on the picked row: Add to document, Copy as user component, Delete from My library.
  - The document component table follows, with the library status and the users of each row: Edit component, Sync from library, Save to My library, Delete from document.
- **Component editor** (`component_edit.rs`): name, insert code (ISO 1832), and the gauge length of a holder with a known built-in shape. "Apply component" is one undoable `EditDocumentComponent`. Each tool built from the part changes in the same undo step.
- **User holders** (`holders.rs`, `holder_view.rs`): a built-in holder has "Copy as user holder". The Holders page lists the user holders of the document above the built-in holders.

title: feat(mcp): tool component library, compatibility and assembly tools
body:
Stacked on #4233. This PR contains the commits of #4233. Merge #4233 first; then this PR takes `git merge origin/main` and a new gate. Do not merge this PR before #4233.

Process change: yes

## What changed

This PR adds eight MCP tools for tool components, tool assemblies and the user component library. The tools are in three new files of `crates/app/src/mcp/`: `component_tools.rs`, `assembly_tools.rs` and `component_library_tools.rs`.

Read tools:
- `list_tool_components`: lists the built-in components, the user library and the document component table. The filters are `kind`, `scope` and `compatible_with`. A row of a match has `fits: [{as, port}]`. A document row has its library sync status.
- `get_tool_assembly`: gives the component stack of a document tool. It gives each node with its mount (parent, port, Z rotation, stickout `projection_mm`), its MCS frame and its sync status. It also gives the derived cutting diameter and corner radius, the gauge length, and the `links` input form.

Document write tools. Each tool runs the same undoable command as the GUI, in one History step:
- `upsert_tool_component` (`UpsertDocumentComponent`)
- `delete_tool_component` (`DeleteDocumentComponent`)
- `set_tool_assembly` (`SetToolAssembly`; `links: null` clears the stack)
- `sync_tool_component` (`SyncDocumentComponent`)

User library tools. These are file edits through `component_library::store`, not undoable commands:
- `save_library_component`
- `delete_library_component`

Each tool validates its arguments early and refuses by name. A component goes through the MCP door in the `.camproj` wire form (`ComponentDto`, `deny_unknown_fields`). A stack goes through as `LinkDto`. A stated `library_ref` in an upsert or a save is refused. A `builtin:` id is refused for a library save and delete. An optional `library` argument names another `.camcomponents` file, as the cut recipe tools do.

Live GUI gate (`mcp/live.rs`): the two library write tools are `FileWrite`. A stated `library` on `list_tool_components`, `get_tool_assembly` and `sync_tool_component` is `FilePathAccess`.

The `camcraft-mcp` skill lists each new tool (section 4). This is a process file, so the body has the line `Process change: yes`. The PR does not change `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.

Decision: `docs/decisions/3647-component-mcp-tools.md`.

Docs: the generated tool reference `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and the user guide `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md` list the new tools. The `mcp_doc_drift` suite pins both.

title: fix(sim): the field simulator cuts a move past the per-move ceiling in pieces, so Stock cuts what the column engine cuts
body:
## What changed

`SdfField::subtract_batch` refuses a chord whose swept window adds more than `MAX_CELLS_PER_MOVE` cells beyond the tool at rest. No caller segmented, so through `Stock` the field engine refused ordinary moves that the column engine cuts.

- `SdfField::subtract_batch_fitted` (new, `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_cut.rs`) is `subtract_batch` with each chord or arc piece whose travel exceeds the ceiling cut as the fewest equal pieces that each fall under it. It finds the count by doubling until the pieces fall under it, then by bisection below that count. A chord splits at equal fractions of its ends. An arc piece splits into equal angular parts on the same circle, with Z shared out evenly (`ArcPiece::split`, `field_arc.rs`). Pieces shorter than one cell shrink no window further, so past that count it refuses by name. A sweep that is neither a chord nor an arc piece cannot be split and refuses by name.
- The six field arms of `Stock` cut through it, one call each: `simulate_field_with` (`backend.rs`), `simulate_undercut` (`field_undercut.rs`), the lathe arm (`field_lathe.rs`), the display arm (`display.rs`), and the single-move `subtract_flat` and `cut_chord` (`backend_edit.rs`).
- `subtract_batch` and `subtract` keep the refusal as the bound of one update. The pin `a_wide_tools_long_chord_still_refuses_and_its_segments_cut` now checks that refusal on `subtract_batch` directly, and checks that `subtract_batch_fitted` cuts the same chord. Its block is now `SdfField::from_box` and it cuts the chord once (5.9 s in debug, from 259 s with three mesh-built fields and two cuts).

Where this differs from the issue: the issue proposed splitting `Move`s in each caller. This PR splits inside the field, at the chord and arc piece, because those are the units the ceiling measures. A move carries an arc, a pose and a C angle, and each caller would need its own interpolation of them. One split there covers every arm. The reasons are in `docs/decisions/4179-segment-to-ceiling.md`.

## Pinning tests

Synthetic blocks only, cell 0.254 mm, all in `crates/sim/tests/field_wide_tool.rs`. For the old code, `subtract_batch_fitted` was made to refuse as `subtract_batch` does, which is main's behaviour through `Stock`:

| Test | Old behaviour | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| `an_endmills_300_mm_pass_cuts_on_both_engines` (the issue's steps) | fails: the field engine refuses | passes |
| `a_127_mm_tools_6_mm_plunge_cuts_on_both_engines` | fails: refused | passes |

| `a_wide_tools_long_chord_still_refuses_and_its_segments_cut` | fails at the fitted chord | passes |
| `the_single_move_stock_arms_cut_the_long_chord` (`subtract_flat`, `cut_chord`) | fails: `subtract_flat` refuses ("segment it") | passes |
| `a_127_mm_tools_helical_entry_cuts_on_both_engines` (arc split) | fails: refused (release) | passes (release, 328 s) |
| `a_wide_tools_short_move_cuts_on_the_field_engine_as_on_the_column_engine` (unchanged) | passes | passes |

The helical test is in the heavy lane (`#[ignore]`): it takes about 22 min in debug, past the 60 s rule in `AGENTS.md`. It was run by hand with `cargo test --release -p camcraft-sim --test field_wide_tool -- --ignored a_127_mm_tools_helical_entry_cuts_on_both_engines`.

title: feat(pathkernel): the load control stage
body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

This PR adds stage 3 of the path kernel (K3): the load control stage. The stage changes guide curves only. It adds no entry, no link and no lift. No old planner changes. With the default switch, the output is identical.

## Public surface (`camcraft_pathkernel::load`)

- `LoadStage` implements `LoadPlanner`. `LoadStage::new(limit)` sets the limit (ae/D) that the stage uses for `None` and `Trochoidal`, which have no limit of their own. `Default` is 0.5 (a 90 degree contact).
- `LoadControl::None`: the set does not change. Each read above `limit x (1 + PLAN_TOL)` gets an `OverLimit` record (`NO_CONTROL`). The verdict has one status line `Note` for each reason, with the count, the worst load and its place.
- `LoadControl::ConstantEngagement` with `Reach::Rings`: the stage inserts a mid-level ring where a ring reads above the load. An insertion that does not lower the load is removed, and the cut gets a name (`NOT_FIXED`, the sharp corner of offset rings). The other names are `FRESH_CUT`, `NOT_A_RING`, `AT_FLOOR` and `TOO_MANY_PASSES`.
- `Reach::Stock` (Adaptive) is refused with `STOCK_REACH_ELSEWHERE`. The HSM planner stays behind the load trait (K0 record, revision 2).
- `LoadControl::Trochoidal`: each `FullWidth` stretch becomes loops that walk the stretch. The free room sets the loop size. If no loop fits, the stretch stays and gets a name. The names are `NO_ROOM`, `LOOPS_OVER` and `NOT_MARKED`. A loop point outside the area is refused (`LOOP_LEAVES`).
- One engagement law for all modes (`load/law.rs`). The stage makes a raster of the `StockRead` stock and reads it in the cut order: ae/D = (1 - cos phi) / 2 at the rim of the swept disc. `NO_RASTER` refuses a region that has no raster.
- A `FullWidth` mark that has no read above the limit is resolved and removed. A mark that stays is named by its reads. `Controlled::new` stays the single gate for law 6.

## Pins

- `camcraft-pathkernel` `laws`, new `load_stage.rs`: the stage runs with the kit, the ring planner (K2), `OrderStage` and `LinkStage` (K4). The fixtures are the disc pocket, the pocket with an island, and two lobes with a neck (a `FullWidth` mark).
  - `k3_none_keeps_the_curves_and_names_every_cut_above_the_limit`
  - `k3_constant_engagement_leaves_no_unnamed_cut_above_the_limit`
  - `k3_trochoidal_leaves_no_full_width_feed_in_the_marked_stretch`
  - `k3_a_stretch_with_no_room_for_a_loop_stays_and_is_named`
  - `k3_an_unnamed_cut_above_the_limit_and_a_bad_limit_are_refused`: an unnamed over-limit read; a limit that is NaN, -0.1, 0 or 1.5; the stock reach; a tool radius that is not a number.
- `camcraft-motion` `kernel_laws`, new `k3_load.rs`: `kernel_load_control_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone`. It uses the law measures of #4154 at a 25 % load. `k4_order_link.rs` gets `kernel_path_with`, which puts a load stage between order and link. The K4 pin does not change.

## Readings (measured, no constant tuned)

Law suite (the check grid of the suite; hot = a read above `load x 1.05`):

| Fixture (load) | Kernel, None: curves / hot reads / worst ae/D | Kernel, constant engagement: curves / hot reads (unnamed) / worst ae/D |
|---|---|---|
| disc pocket (0.25) | 4 / 3 / 0.413 | 9 / 0 (0) / 0.179 |
| pocket with an island (0.20) | 12 / 286 / 0.999 | 29 / 146 (0) / 0.998 |
| two lobes and a neck (0.40) | 9 / 249 / 0.998 | 27 / 128 (0) / 0.998 |

Trochoidal on the neck: the worst read in the marked stretch is 0.941. Before, it was 1.0 (full width). All loops stay in the cutter-centre area.

Motion `kernel_laws` (#4154 meter, limit 60 degrees, the band round the part). Each cell gives the feed moves above the limit, the worst angle in degrees, and the moves above the limit with no named place within one tool radius:

| Case | Old 2D Pocket | Kernel without load control (None) | Kernel with constant engagement |
|---|---|---|---|
| disc Inside | 20 / 178 / all | 3507 / 173 / 0 | 833 / 173 / 1 |
| disc Outside | 20 / 178 / all | 402 / 145 / 13 | 334 / 118 / 74 |
| dog bone Inside | 32 / 180 / all | 2587 / 173 / 0 | 581 / 173 / 1 |
| dog bone Outside | 32 / 180 / all | 724 / 167 / 3 | 678 / 143 / 66 |

- The kernel counts each short move of its dense rings. Thus its counts and the old counts do not compare one to one. The first K4 reading was over 3504 on the disc Inside. It is 3507 on this base.
- The worst value Inside (173 degrees) is the first ring round the part. It is a full-width cut with no pass beside it, and it is named (`FRESH_CUT`).
- The unnamed moves on the Outside rows are on the stock edge line, where a piece starts after a lift. There the kernel read and the #4154 meter differ. Follow-up: #4260 (P7). The one unnamed move on each Inside row is a link feed (stage 5).

## Decisions

`docs/decisions/4026-kernel-load-control.md`. In short:
- The stage has a limit of its own for `None` and `Trochoidal`.
- Constant engagement inserts passes. It does not make a new spiral or a new ladder.
- The stock reach is refused by name.
- The trochoid walks the stretch, and the free room sets its size.
- The reader reads after the clear, outside the edge. The first form read inside the edge and gave values that were too low (54 degrees where the geometry gives 64).

## Gates on the final head

- `cargo check --tests -p camcraft-pathkernel` and `-p camcraft-motion`: pass.
- `camcraft-pathkernel --test laws`: 130 passed.
- `camcraft-motion --test kernel_laws`: 30 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-pathkernel --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `-p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel`: 4 steps, all ok (pathkernel lib, pathkernel laws, motion kernel_laws).
- `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work` of camcraft-app: 43 passed (4 ignored), 1 passed, 1 passed.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 7 steps, all ok (motion light lib and `adaptive_troch_island`, `_neck`, `_parallel`; app light `pocket_pass_start`, `offset_pass_start`).

## Not exercised

- No kind plans on the kernel yet. The registry table does not change. Each K6 group moves its kinds.
- Constant engagement with the stock reach (Adaptive): refused by this stage.
- Trochoidal on a fixture of #3932 with an open edge and a near wall. The loops walk the marked stretch, but no pin uses that fixture.
- The #3849 law is covered by construction: each curve is read, and the clean-up rings too (`each_curve_read`). There is no clean-up fixture of #1587.
- The loop sense from climb or conventional. A microlift return between loops (stage 5).
- The tool shapes that are not a disc. The lathe plane.

title: feat(tools)!: .camtools version 8 carries tool components and stacks
body:
Stacked on #4233. This PR contains the commits of #4233. Merge #4233 first; then this PR takes `git merge origin/main` and a new gate. Do not merge this PR before #4233.

## What changed

This is slice 2 of #3645: the `.camtools` export and import of tool components and tool stacks.

- `.camtools` version 8 (`ASSEMBLY_VERSION`):
  - A definition of an assembled tool holds its stack as `assembly`. These are the `project::assembly_wire` links, as a `.camproj` tool states them.
  - The file holds a top-level `components` array with the rows that the exported stacks name. The rows use the wire form of `project::component_wire` from #4233.
  - The version step is conditional. A library without a stack keeps its older number (1 to 7) and the same bytes.
- Strict reading (`crates/app/src/tool_library/assembly.rs`):
  - The table is read whole. Each row is built again and refused by its id.
  - Each stack must name rows of the table and resolve, or the file is refused by the tool name.
  - A row that no stack names is refused by its id.
  - A file of version 7 or older that states `components` or `assembly` is refused.
  - The body of an assembled tool goes through `as_derived`, as on a project open (new `project::stack_from_dto`).
- Import (`crates/app/src/commands/tool_import/`):
  - `ImportTools` lands the rows and the tools in its one undo step. The table changes first on apply and is restored last on undo.
  - The rows land in the order of the file table, so an export after the import gives the same bytes.
  - An added or renamed tool gets its stack. An updated or replaced tool takes the library stack. A library tool without a stack clears the old stack on update, because the record does not come from that stack any more.
  - "Holders off" leaves out the stacks and their rows with the bodies.
  - `ImportReport` names the added and the reused rows.
  - The number laws moved to `tool_import/numbers.rs` without a change, to keep `mod.rs` below 400 lines.
- The id rule (`docs/decisions/3645-camtools-v8.md`). A library row whose id the document already holds:
  - same content (name, item, geometry): the document row is reused;
  - different content: the import is refused by the id, and nothing lands.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders/camtools_v8.rs` (a new submodule of the existing `tool_library_holders` suite; no new top-level binary):

- `an_export_of_assembled_tools_is_version_8_and_imports_identically`
- `a_library_of_plain_tools_keeps_its_older_number_and_imports_as_before`
- `a_newer_version_and_an_older_file_with_components_are_refused`
- `a_bad_row_a_bad_link_or_an_unused_row_refuses_the_file_by_name`
- `undo_and_redo_of_an_import_with_components_restore_tools_and_table`
- `a_document_row_of_the_same_id_is_reused_when_the_same_and_refuses_when_different`

## Gate results (head `26eab082f`)

The base of the quick gate is the head of #4233 (`745234df7`). All runs are local, on the Mac.

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base 745234df7`), at `323e1430a`: 200 steps, 198 ok, 2 red. The red steps were `holder_reference` and `tool_library`. Their tests named version 8 as the first unknown number. The fix moves them to version 9.
- The red steps again (`--failed`) on the fix: 2 ok.
- On the final head `26eab082f` (the only later change is a `type` alias for clippy and the test fix): `app suites: tool_library_holders`, `tool_library`, `holder_reference`, `tool_import_modes`, `tool_table`: all ok. The pinning tests (`gate test camtools_v8`): 6 ok.
- Strict clippy (`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`) on the final head: clean.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`) on the final head: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- Example catalog suites: not needed. No post and no toolpath changed. They are in the quick plan and were ok.

## Not exercised

- The MCP reply and the UI import page do not show the component counts yet. The MCP tools are #3647 and the UI is #3648.
- A stack in the bare `[{name, definition}]` array is refused, because that form has no table.

Changelog: `.camtools` tool libraries now carry tool components and tool assemblies (version 8). The import adds the components in the same undo step, reuses a component of the same content, and refuses a different component of the same id.

title: fix(pathkernel): a link can run outside the stock where the ground is proved
body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

Sub-PR of the path kernel (#4023), K4b. Writer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/4241#issuecomment-7206326747

## The rule

A link sample can stand in the cutter-centre area, in the air, or in the edge band. The edge band is the band outside the stock within one tool radius of a stock edge. The link stage reads it from the legal room of the entry stage (`entry::legal_room`, K5). There is no second definition.

A sample in the edge band must also:
- not be inside the part zone (the part grown by the tool radius plus the stock to leave), so that the disc meets no part;
- be more than a tool radius from each keep-out area (else `HITS_FIXTURE`).

The part of the disc inside the stock is stock as any other. The swath test of K4 does not change: a sample that is not in the air must be within 0.9 tool radius of a cut already made (else `UNCUT_STOCK`). The old meaning "outside the stock by 0.1 r counts as air" is not ported.

## What changed

- `crates/pathkernel/src/link/proof.rs`: the chord proof accepts a sample in the edge band (`in_band`). The legal room is built once for each proof, at the first sample outside the centre area and the air.
- `crates/pathkernel/src/link/route.rs`: the edge route also walks along the loops of the air: out through the band, along the air, back in. Each chord is proved as before.
- `crates/pathkernel/src/region.rs`, `region_build.rs`: an `Outside` region keeps its part zone (`part_zone`, set by the builder only). The air now leaves out the part zone. Before, a part that reaches out of the stock was in the air, and the proof accepted a link in the air across it.
- `crates/pathkernel/src/entry/room.rs`, `entry/mod.rs`: `legal_room` is `pub(crate)`, so that the link stage reads the same room.
- The link law (`tests/laws/link_rule.rs`, `check_link`) reads the edge band too, from the stock of the case and not from the kernel's room.

No old planner changes. With the default switch the output is identical. The kernel still depends only on `camcraft-geometry`. The plan's transition table and the link stage stay the single gates.

## Pins

Negative first (`crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/link_rule.rs`):
- `a_link_in_the_edge_band_over_uncut_stock_is_refused`: `UNCUT_STOCK`.
- `a_link_in_the_edge_band_near_a_keep_out_is_refused`: `HITS_FIXTURE` (a clamp outside the stock).
- `a_link_beside_a_part_that_reaches_out_of_the_stock_is_refused`: `CUTS_PART`; also no stay link across the part in the air.

Positive:
- `a_link_leaves_a_cut_at_the_stock_edge_runs_in_the_air_and_comes_back_over_cleared_stock`: stays at depth through the air. Without the cut made at the next start, the same link is refused with `UNCUT_STOCK`.

## Counts before and after (measured again, no constant changed)

Law suite `order_link::k4_link_rule_holds_and_each_lift_is_named` (Auto / Inside / Outside) and motion pin `kernel_order_and_link_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone` (lifts, crossing feeds):

| Fixture | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| disc pocket (law suite) | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| disc band (law suite) | 13 / 0 / 13 | 13 / 0 / 13 |
| dog-bone band (law suite) | 15 / 0 / 15 | 15 / 0 / 15 |
| pocket with an island (law suite) | 7 / 7 / 5 | 7 / 7 / 5 |
| disc Inside (motion) | 0 lifts, 0 crossings | 0 lifts, 0 crossings |
| disc Outside (motion) | 13 lifts, 0 crossings | 13 lifts, 0 crossings |
| dog bone Inside (motion) | 0 lifts, 0 crossings | 0 lifts, 0 crossings |
| dog bone Outside (motion) | 15 lifts, 0 crossings | 15 lifts, 0 crossings |

The target of 0 lifts on the disc is not met. Each of the 13 lifts on the disc band (Outside) is at the start of a piece that no cut has touched yet. The way in to that start runs over stock that is not within the swath of a cut made:
- 4 `UNCUT_STOCK`: in a corner, from piece k on the long edge to piece k - 1 on the short edge. The next start is 4.4 mm or more from each cut made (the swath is 3.6 mm).
- 4 `CUTS_PART`: from piece k (k = 7, 6) on one long edge to piece k - 1 on the other long edge. The straight link crosses the part; back along the cut, the next start is 3.98 mm and 5.47 mm from the cut made.
- 5 `CROSSES_CUT`: from the last piece of a group to the first piece of the next group. The straight link crosses cuts; the way round through the air is proved out and along the air, but not back in to the first piece of the new group.

The decision says which rule can remove these lifts (an approach from the air proved as a lead-in). That changes the link rule, so it is not done here.

## Decision

`docs/decisions/4241-kernel-link-edge-band.md`.

## Gate (final head)

- `cargo check --tests -p camcraft-pathkernel`: pass.
- `cargo check --tests -p camcraft-motion`: pass.
- `camcraft-pathkernel` `laws` suite: 129 passed.
- `camcraft-motion` `kernel_laws` suite: 29 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-pathkernel -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel`: pass, 4 steps (pathkernel lib, pathkernel `laws`, motion `kernel_laws` `k4_order_link::`), 0 failed, 0 stalled

## Not exercised

- The light lane and the heavy lanes (no planner calls the kernel; a P7 PR runs no heavy step).
- The `example_catalog*` suites: no post and no old toolpath changed.
- A stock with more than one outline loop. The part zone covers it by construction, but no fixture has one.
- The entry stage with a part that reaches out of the stock: its air room gets smaller there, and no entry pin has such a part.

This PR is the app part of #3646. It builds on the #4201 component commands. It does not depend on PR #4233, and it does not touch `crates/app/src/project/`.

The running data of the insert goes on each tool that cuts with that insert. This includes the single-seat insert path.
- `UpsertDocumentComponent::with_row` and `EditDocumentComponent::with_row` take the whole row. `EditDocumentComponent::new` keeps the facts and the running data of the held row. The command refuses a fact on the wrong kind of component when the row is made. It also refuses running rows that a milling tool cannot take.

title: feat(wire): control and wear wire offset for Wire Contour (COMP records for the LN2W post)
body:
Process change: yes

## What changed

- A Wire Contour has a new parameter, `compensation`: `computer` (the default, as before), `control` or `wear`.
- The generator makes and judges the same wire-centre path as before. With `control` or `wear`, each pass then gets one `CompSpan` (`motion::wire_edm::wire_comp_spans`, a new module `comp.rs`).
  - Control: the span's programmed geometry is the part contour. Each ring move moves back by the offset along its normal. A line moves by translation, an arc keeps its centre and changes its radius. Two lines at a mitred joint meet at the part corner. A corner round that the offset put in collapses to its corner.
  - Wear: the programmed geometry is the wire-centre walk itself.
  - Each span states its pass's kerf offset (wire radius plus the gap of the pass's condition) as its radius. The rough pass is first, then each skim.
- The post dump already writes a span between `COMP` records (M13.11). So the LN2W post of #4139 writes `G41` / `G42 Hnnn` by pass, with `C001` and `H001` first, and `G40` on each lead-out. The post and the engine do not change.
- The command door (`wire_gate`) and the generator refuse control or wear by name with: an open run, a 4-axis cut, a taper, a burnout, tabs, the arc lead, an exit pick (`operation::wire_comp::refusal`).
- The span builder refuses by name: a lead-in or lead-out shorter than the pass's offset, an arc lead, a pass that does not return to the start hole, a hairpin turn, an arc at a sharp joint.
- Mark 21, G-EDM and the other wire posts refuse the offset by name (their existing hooks, or the engine's refusal).
- Project file: the key `compensation` is written only when it is not `computer`. The stamp digests it only then. No existing file or stamp changes.
- MCP: the parameter rides the operation DTO, so `add_operation` and `edit_operation` take it. `list_operation_types` lists it. The `camcraft-mcp` skill row names it (a process file: `Process change: yes`).
- Each `WireContourOp` literal in the tests gets `compensation: Default::default()`.

## Cause

`posting_wire.rs` posted only the wire-centre path, and the op had no mode. No LN2W program with the control's offset could come from the app (#4134).

## Item 3 of the issue: how the wire laws judge the path

The kerf, threading and slug laws judge the wire-centre moves, as before. These moves are what the control cuts when each register holds the radius that its span states. The post writes that radius in the comment before each `G41` / `G42` line (`THE STREAM STATES 0.165 MM`). The decision is in `docs/decisions/4134-wire-control-offset.md`.

## Tests

Pins (all new):

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `wire_edm::comp::tests` (9): `a_die_square_is_programmed_on_its_profile_under_g41`, `a_punch_square_is_programmed_on_its_profile_under_g42`, `a_reversed_skim_takes_the_other_side`, `each_pass_states_its_own_radius`, `the_wear_span_programs_the_wire_centre_moves`, `computer_compensation_records_nothing`, `a_circle_is_programmed_as_arcs_at_the_part_radius`, `a_lead_in_shorter_than_the_offset_is_refused_by_name`, `an_arc_lead_and_an_open_run_are_refused_by_name`.
- `camcraft-app` `wire_post`, `sodick_aq600l::offset` (5): `the_ln2w_square_posts_the_part_contour_with_the_controls_offset`, `the_ln2w_two_axis_block_posts_the_part_arcs_with_the_controls_offset`, `the_ln2w_square_posts_the_wire_centre_path_with_a_wear_offset`, `the_mark_21_post_refuses_the_controls_offset_by_name`, `the_offset_with_a_taper_or_an_open_run_is_refused_at_the_door`.
- `camcraft-app` lib, `the_wire_compensation_round_trips_and_is_absent_for_computer`.
- `mcp_wire_contour::list_operation_types_and_skill_match_wire_contour_dto_and_tool_law` now includes `compensation`.

Red before the fix: the pins do not compile on `upstream/main` (no `compensation` field, no `wire_comp_spans`).

Mutations (each run, then restored, then green):

- Generation hook removed (`generate.rs` from `upstream/main`): 4 of 5 `offset` pins red (the door pin stays green, as it must).
- Door refusal removed (`gates.rs`): `the_offset_with_a_taper_or_an_open_run_is_refused_at_the_door` red.

Side branch: side/path-kernel

Sub-PR 2 of 2 for #4176 (K2, the guide stage). Sub-PR 1 (the ring and row planners) merged as PR #4189. This PR adds the medial line, the trace of a chain and the helix guide planners. No old planner changes. No planner calls the new code yet, so with the default switch the output is identical. The baseline pins of the side branch stay green.

## Public surface

- `guide::MedialPlanner`: the medial axis of the cutter-centre area, family `Medial`. Refusals: `NO_MEDIAL`, `NARROW_NECK`, `MEDIAL_TOO_FINE`, `NOT_MEDIAL`.

- `TraceOffset`: above zero is to the left of the chain. A closed chain is read counter-clockwise, so its left is its inside.

- `Guides` plans each family. `FAMILY_NOT_YET` is removed. The area planners refuse a chain region with `NOT_AN_AREA`.
- New in `camcraft-geometry`, each in its own file:
  - `Region::medial_axis`, `Region::medial_spacing`, `MedialAxis`, `MedialCurve` (`geo2d/medial.rs`, with a crate-private Delaunay in `geo2d/delaunay.rs`);

The guide choices moved from `guide.rs` to `guide/choice.rs` with no change. The public paths stay the same by re-export.

title: fix(post): Heidenhain PECK and DEEP post the checked chain
body:
## What changed

The Heidenhain DIN/ISO post (`assets/posts/heidenhain.cps`) now writes PECK and DEEP holes as the expanded chain in plain `G00` / `G01` blocks. This occurs at each R clearance. The post writes no `G205` and no peck `G200`.

- The old `G205` had `Q257` = `Q202` = the peck and `Q258=0`. The control made a full retract after each infeed, then moved at FMAX to the cut face.
- The old peck `G200` had `Q200=0`. The control moved at FMAX to the last depth.
- The chain makes chip-break hops (PECK), or rapids to R and feeds down from R (DEEP). The simulation and the gouge check read the chain. The posted blocks are now that chain, move for move.
- DRILL and SPOT keep `G200`, with `Q202` = the whole depth (one infeed). Taps keep `G206` / `G207`.
- The `Q208` retract-feed code was only for `G205`, so this PR removes it. The `Q395` level guard of `G200` stays. A test pins its refusal.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/4224-heidenhain-peck-chain.md`. It gives what was chosen, why, and what was dropped. A corrected native `G205` was dropped: the cited manuals do not prove its motion equal to the chain.

## Readings

Golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/heidenhain/drill_peck.nc`, block N100 and after:

N110 G00 X+20 Y+10 Z-17*

## What changed

This is the first slice of #3919. The built-in holder library gets seven more tapers. Each taper has ER collet chucks and Weldon side-lock holders. - `crates/tools/src/holder_library_hsk.rs`: HSK-A63, HSK-F63, HSK-E40, HSK-E32 (DIN 69893-1 / -5 / -6). The plane face is the gauge line. The collar (f1) is drawn as a full cylinder at d1.

- `docs/decisions/3919-standard-holders.md`: each number and its source, the entry list, and what this slice leaves out.

Numbers (mm):

| Taper | Flange Ø | Standoff | Flange / collar | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SK30, ISO30 | 50 | 3.2 | 15.9 | Haimer DIN ISO 7388-1 table; "SK40_DIN69871.pdf" data sheet; Techniks router catalog (ISO30 Ø50) |
| SK40 | 63.55 | 3.2 | 15.9 | the same two tables |

title: fix(app): the stock export judges the mesh as the file holds it; the written-corner weld settles duplicates by edge parity
body:
## What changed

A binary STL writes each corner as f32. Corners closer than one f32 step become one corner in the file, so a stock mesh that passed the closed check in f64 could be written with repeated corners and edges not on two facets.

- `stock_export::file_bytes` (new, `crates/app/src/stock_export.rs`) judges the mesh as the file will hold it: it rounds the corners to their written f32 values (`repair::weld_at_f32`). When a facet collapses at those values, or two distinct corners round to one, it welds bit-exact and checks the result with `unpaired_edges`, refusing by name if the written mesh would not be closed. A mesh with nothing to collapse writes byte for byte as before. `write_stl` and the UI's stock export (`crates/ui/src/state.rs`, same line count) use it.
- In that written-corner weld only, duplicate facets settle by edge parity (`duplicate_sets` with `Duplicates::ByParity`): a set of copies whose edges the rest of the mesh uses an even number of times keeps no copy; otherwise the first copy stays. Keeping one copy of a back-to-back pair left that pair's three edges on one facet each.
- `repair::weld`, which `RepairModel` runs on a part model, keeps main's rule (`Duplicates::KeepFirst`): the first copy of each duplicate set stays. The first version of this PR used parity there too, and review found that it removed double-sided surfaces of a part model (finding 1). The export's input is a closed surface, so a duplicate set there can only be two faces the rounding laid together.

Why parity and not the issue's "k mod 2" (keep a copy when the count is odd): k mod 2 removes a single stray duplicate on a closed solid (k = 2), which the existing pin `drop_degenerate` keeps (a flipped duplicate on a cube stays as one copy). Parity keeps that case as pinned and removes the back-to-back pair the weld leaves.

The decision is in `docs/decisions/4182-stl-as-written.md`.

## Pinning tests

Synthetic shapes only.
- `crates/app/tests/stock_export.rs` `the_exported_file_is_closed_as_written_and_a_clean_mesh_writes_unchanged`: on main `e6849c5ae` with only the test added it fails, facets written left `6`, right `4`. On this branch it passes.
- `crates/app/tests/stock_export.rs` `two_solids_whose_edges_meet_in_the_file_are_refused`: on head `025f59e36` (no corner-meet check) it fails, the bytes are written. On this branch it is refused by name.
- `crates/app/tests/stock_export.rs` `a_sliver_that_collapses_to_nothing_as_written_is_refused`: passes on this branch (refused, "collapses to nothing").
- `crates/geometry/tests/repair.rs` `a_back_to_back_pair_left_at_the_written_corners_goes_and_the_mesh_stays_closed`: through `weld_at_f32`, the thin tetrahedron gives (triangles after, dropped) `(0, 4)` and no open edge. With one copy kept, it was `(1, 3)` and open (the reviewer's mutation M1 on `025f59e36`).
- `crates/geometry/tests/repair.rs` `corners_closer_than_an_f32_step_weld_at_their_written_values`: passes on this branch.
- `crates/app/tests/repair_model.rs` `a_double_sided_sheet_keeps_its_facets_through_repair` and `a_double_sided_fin_on_a_cube_stays_through_repair` (finding 1): on `025f59e36`'s repair both fail. The sheet is refused ("would update the model to empty geometry"), and the fin cube drops 4 facets, where 2 is expected. On this branch both pass.

On this branch: repair 12 tests, repair_model 7, stock_export 5, all pass.

## Gates

On head `217de3194` (base upstream/main `1c0152c91`):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 1226 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (101.5 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: green, 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (34.2 min).
- No heavy step: this is not a `P1`. No post or toolpath changed, so no example catalog suite.

On the first head `025f59e36` the quick gate was green (1226 steps, 128.5 min) and the light lane green (6 steps, 65.8 min).

Trial merge with upstream/main `903e420b3`: clean (`git merge-tree`).

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes.
- A mesh whose f32 collapse leaves a non-manifold edge that bit-exact welding cannot settle, other than the two solids whose edges meet: `file_bytes` refuses it by name.
- `RepairModel` on other double-sided shapes: the pins cover a sheet and a fin; `weld` is main's code path for every caller.
- In our own lane (outside this repository), two cut stock meshes that were closed in f64 showed 3 to 6 edges on 3 or more facets and 4 to 8 zero-area facets as written. Those meshes are not attached; the pins above are the evidence here.

Effort: high (stock export of simulated stock).

title: feat(pathkernel): the order stage and the link stage
body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

K4 of the path kernel (#4023): the order stage and the link stage, behind `OrderPlanner` and `LinkProof`. No old planner changes. No planner calls the new code yet, so the output with the default switch is identical.

## What changed

Public surface:
- `order::OrderStage` (impl `OrderPlanner`). It resolves Auto, gets the sense of the walk from the region, sets climb or conventional for each curve, and picks the order and the start points. Refusal: `ORDER_NOT_PLANAR`.
- `OrderedSet::marks()`. `OrderedSet::new` moves each mark of the guide set to the new index of its curve. A stretch on a reversed curve is reversed too. No planner can drop a mark.
- `link::LinkStage` (impl `LinkProof`). The tool stays down on a proved path, else it lifts with a named reason.
- `link::Level { made, planned, links }` (`Level::new`, `with_links`). `LinkProof::link` now takes a `Level` instead of `planned: &[Cut]`.
- Lift reasons: `CUTS_PART`, `HITS_FIXTURE`, `CROSSES_CUT`, `UNCUT_STOCK`, `BAD_PATH`, `NOT_PLANAR_LINK` (and the existing `USER_RETRACT`). Constant: `SWATH` = 0.9. Each lift arm has its own named reason, with no fallback.
- `camcraft-geometry`: `geo2d::segments_cross`, `segment_gap` and `point_segment_distance`, each with unit tests. The kernel still depends on geometry only.

Order (`crates/pathkernel/src/order/`):
- A ring waits for the neighbour rings on the side that the walk comes from (the order of the offset tree, Held 1991).
- From the ready starts, the walk takes the first one that the link stage can prove. It tries them in this order: curves without a full-width stretch first, then the next run on the chain of the Adaptive air plan (`air_chain::chains`, ported), then the nearest start.

Link (`crates/pathkernel/src/link/`): the stage tries three paths, in order:
1. The straight chord.
2. Back along the open cut just made, then a chord to the next start (`air_chain::link`, ported).
3. A walk along a loop of the centre area (`ring_links::edge_route`, ported).

Each chord must stay in the centre area or the air. It must not touch a planned cut and must not cross a made cut or an earlier link. It may run only over cleared stock: within 0.9 tool radius of a made cut, or in the air of the region. The strip just inside the stock edge is stock as any other: it is open only where the swath of a made cut covers it (review of this PR). If no path is proved, the hop lifts with the reason of the straight chord. The table in `Plan::new` stays the one gate.

## Readings: old against new

Motion `kernel_laws` with the #4154 measures, tool radius 4, step 2:

| Fixture | Kernel lifts / crossing feeds | Old 2D Pocket | Old 2D Offset |
|---|---|---|---|
| disc Inside | 0 / 0 | 18, none named / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| disc Outside | 13, named / 0 | 18, none named / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| dog bone Inside | 0 / 0 | 26, none named / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| dog bone Outside | 15, named / 0 | 26, none named / 0 | 0 / 0 |

The tried level blend of #3934 gave 35 lifts on the disc and 24 crossing feeds on the dog bone. The kernel gives 0 crossing feeds. The first head of this PR read 0 lifts on Outside too, but only because the edge strip counted as open ground, which is not proved. Outside starts at the stock edge. The link from one piece there to the next runs over the strip that the next piece cuts, and the kernel cannot leave the stock into the air (its air starts one tool radius outside the stock). Follow-up: #4241.

Law suite: 0 lifts on the disc pocket (Auto, Inside, Outside) and on the two bands Inside. The disc band lifts 13 times on Auto and Outside (5 `CROSSES_CUT`, 4 `UNCUT_STOCK`, 4 `CUTS_PART`). The dog-bone band lifts 15 times on Auto and Outside (13 `CROSSES_CUT`, 2 `UNCUT_STOCK`). The pocket with an island has 7 lifts (Inside and Auto) and 5 lifts (Outside), each with a named reason:
- Inside: the four corners are four separate deepest areas. The link between two corners runs over a strip that is not cut yet, or across a ring that is still planned.
- Outside: the walk must go from the wall rings to the island rings, across the rings that are still planned between them.

The engagement readings are higher than the old ones (for example `over 3504` on the disc Inside: the rings run outward from the part wall, and each move of the dense rings counts). This step does not change the load. Load control is K3.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/order_link.rs`:
  - `k4_order_obeys_l3_with_the_ring_planner`
  - `k4_link_rule_holds_and_each_lift_is_named` (pins the lift counts)
  - `a_link_across_the_island_is_refused_with_the_part_reason`
  - `a_link_round_the_island_stays_on_cut_ground_only`
  - `a_lift_with_no_reason_is_refused_and_a_retract_is_named`
  - `an_order_that_moves_a_curve_is_refused`
  - `the_side_orders_the_rings_and_climb_keeps_the_material_on_the_right`
  - `the_marks_go_with_their_curves_and_a_full_width_stretch_is_cut_last`
  - `a_link_along_the_stock_edge_over_uncut_stock_is_refused` (review fix)
  - `a_whole_full_width_curve_is_cut_after_the_other_ready_curves` (review fix)
  - `a_row_on_the_first_step_keeps_its_direction_and_the_next_rows_zigzag` (review fix)
- `crates/motion/tests/kernel_laws/k4_order_link.rs`: `kernel_order_and_link_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone` (0 crossings, named lifts equal to the lifts, tally equal to the lifts, the lift counts).
- `crates/geometry/src/geo2d/segments.rs` unit tests, and `link::route` unit tests.

## Gates (final head d50f14a54)

- Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel` (25f3838db). The geometry change reaches every crate, so the plan is the full batch. Result: 1223 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 73.9 min. It includes clippy `-D warnings`, `pathkernel suites: laws`, `motion suites: kernel_laws` and `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`, all ok.
- Separately on the same tree: `cargo check --tests` for `camcraft-pathkernel` and `camcraft-motion`; `laws` 125 passed; pathkernel lib 5 passed; `kernel_laws` 29 passed; clippy `-D warnings` on pathkernel and motion, clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light` ran on the first head (7 steps, 0 failed). The review fix changes only the kernel, which no planner calls yet, so the light twins do not reach it. Not run again.

## Decisions

`docs/decisions/4177-kernel-order-link.md` has the decisions in full. In short:
- A full-width stretch is cut last: last of the ready curves, and a closed curve starts where its longest full-width stretch ends.
- The sense of the walk comes from the region.
- Climb keeps the uncut material on the right.
- The edge strip of the stock is stock: open only where the swath of a made cut covers it (the `AIR` margin is removed).
- A curve that is full-width as a whole comes after the other ready curves and starts as a plain curve. A row on the first step is never reversed.
- These were not ported: the lifted joins of `air_links`, and the stay-down length limit.

## Not exercised

- Rows (Zigzag): one order pin (first row and zigzag) on hand-made rows, none with the row planner. The Fallback note for a start side on Zigzag is not added.
- Exact circle rings and `RingRef::Band`: both are still refused by K2.
- Keep-out areas (`HITS_FIXTURE`): no fixture pin.
- The order stage runs the link proof on each step. Its cost on large parts is not measured.
- No app or UI path calls the kernel yet.

New top-level test files: none. The pins join the `laws` suite and the `kernel_laws` suite.

title: feat(tools)!: component library store and project persistence
body:
Stacked on #4201. This PR adds three commits on top of it: `8fd0a47ec..745234df7`.

## What changed

This is slice 1 of #3645.

- **Project file v84.** A `.camproj` now holds the document tool component table (`components`). Each tool can also hold its component stack (`assembly`).
  - The loader reads the table and each stack before any world write.
  - Each link must name a row, and each stack must resolve (the #3643 resolver). If not, the file is refused by the tool name or the component id.
  - The loader lands the rows and stacks through `table_set` and `set_assembly`. This replaces the clear-on-open line of #4201.
  - The derived `ToolDef` and `ToolBody` stay as the file states them, so an open does not change a posted program.
  - An assembled body gets its source and the judged resolver bands back when its drawn outline is the outline that the stack resolves to (`assembly_wire::as_derived`).
- **One wire form for a component row** (`project::component_wire`), for the project and the library. The codes are written as text: the ISO 1832 insert code, the connection codes, and the ISO 5608 seat letters. The geometry holds the port frames, the body, the cutting point and the bore stops. Each record is read strictly: an unknown key is refused, each row is built again through the checked constructors, and each refusal names the row.
- **`library_ref { id, content_hash }`** on a document row. The hash is FNV-1a 64 over the wire JSON of the name, the item and the geometry.
- **User component library** (`component_library`, `component_library::store`):
  - The file format is `camcraft-components/1` with `units: "mm"`.
  - The folder is `CAMCRAFT_COMPONENTS` (an absolute path). If it is not set, the folder is `<platform data dir>/camcraft/components`. The file is `components.camcomponents`.
  - A save writes a temp file, then renames it.
  - The read is all or nothing. The holder library (each entry with a taper) and the starter tool catalog are read-only built-ins in the `builtin:` id space.
- **Sync.** `sync_status` returns `NotLinked`, `UpToDate`, `UpdateAvailable` or `MissingFromLibrary`. It never applies a library copy.
  - `SyncDocumentComponent` (undoable) puts the library copy into the row, records the link, and derives each user tool again in one undo step through the `EditDocumentComponent` law (`with_row`).
  - A hand edit keeps the link.
  - A change of the link alone derives no tool again.

Decision: `docs/decisions/3645-component-library.md`.

## Compatibility

- `PROJECT_VERSION` goes from 83 to 84. Each file that this build writes says v84, so a v83 build refuses it and cannot drop the table. Files of v83 and older open unchanged. This includes #2016 / PR #2092 `holder` references. The commit is `feat(tools)!:` with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer, as for the v82 and v83 steps and as the issue asks.
- The `.camtools` format does not change in this PR.

## Readings

- The round trip is byte-stable. The project has six component rows and three assembled tools: two indexable cutters with a shared insert, and one solid end mill in an adapter in a holder (two bodies united band by band).
- A turned port frame (`x = [0.6, 0.8, 0]`) reads back to the same bits.

## Pinning tests

All the tests are in the existing directory suite `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders/`. No new top-level test file.

- `component_files::a_project_with_a_component_table_and_its_assemblies_reopens_identically`
- `component_files::a_file_without_a_table_and_a_holder_project_open_unchanged`
- `component_files::a_reader_of_an_older_version_refuses_the_new_file`
- `component_files::a_corrupt_row_or_link_refuses_the_file_by_name`
- `component_sync::the_store_round_trips_and_refuses_a_bad_file_whole_by_name`
- `component_sync::the_save_is_atomic_and_the_env_folder_comes_first`
- `component_sync::the_built_ins_are_the_holders_and_the_starter_tools_read_only`
- `component_sync::a_sync_pulls_a_newer_library_copy_into_both_assemblies_and_undo_restores`
- `component_sync::a_library_copy_that_differs_after_an_open_is_reported_never_applied`

## Gate

All results are on the final head `745234df789bf856404422bcd1e9202e87be85d2` (Mac).

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 363 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (28.3 min). This includes `tool_library_holders`, `project_roundtrip`, `continuous_4axis_part`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` and the ui suites (`ui suites: machine` too).
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed. This ran on head `b376f74fa`. The only later commit is a one-line clippy fix in a test file.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No heavy step: this is a P6 PR.
- The first quick run was void, because a golden regeneration moved the tree during the run. Its one red step was `continuous_4axis_part`: the committed example project pins `PROJECT_VERSION`. The example now says v84 and changes nothing else. The committed `.nc` program stays as it is.

## Not exercised

- The real platform data folder. The tests use a temp folder and the pure `user_dir_for`.
- A lathe assembly. `derive` still refuses it (#3643).

## What is left

- On #3645: `.camtools` with components and assemblies. The issue says v5, but `main` is at version 7 (`CUTTER_HAND_VERSION`), so the step is version 8. The import must land the rows through the `ImportTools` undo unit (`commands/tool_import`).
- #3647: the MCP tools, including `SyncDocumentComponent` and the sync status. No new MCP issue is filed: #3647 covers the component commands.

A user component library (`components.camcomponents`) holds your own components next to the built-in holders and starter tools. An explicit, undoable sync pulls a library change into a project. body:
**Stacked on #4221** (the 2D slice of #1122, which is stacked on #4220 and #4218). The 2D slice names five fields that this guard finds. Until the chain merges, this diff also shows the commits of the three parents (42ca7bfc5, 9886fef31, b852d7257). The commit of this PR is cf3565107. After each parent merges, I merge `main` into this branch.

## What changed

Slice 3 of #1119: the operation pages. Each input on each operation page tab now has an accessible name.

- **The cause.** On `main` 773736856, 1,840 of 1,861 input occurrences on the operation pages had no name. `num` and `combo` set no `labelled_by`. Only the `*_row` variants did, and the pages call the base helpers.
- **A property row names its controls.** `prop_row` opens its row while it draws the row's controls (`layout::named_by`). The seam's fields drawn inside the row take its label as their name (`layout::name_by_row`). These fields are:
  - `num` and its variants, and `num_plain`;
  - `value_with_unit`;
  - `combo`, `combo_owned` and `tool_combo`;
  - `drag_row` (from #4221).

  A field outside an open row takes no name from the seam. Thus a field never takes the name of the row drawn before it, which `row_label_id` (the last row of the frame) could give.
- **The operation header** is a `Grid` with its own labels. Its Tool, Source, Setup and Coolant combos are named through `named_by` with their row labels.
- **Spindle speed** (`spindle_row.rs`) is named by its row.
- **No label twice.** `num_row`, `num_feed_row`, `num_plain_row` and `num_unit_row` already named by the row. They are now the same field as their bases, so no field has the same label two times.
- **Files.** The helpers are in the new file `layout/row_name.rs` (49 lines). `layout/form.rs` grows by 4 lines (420 to 424). It was over the 400-line limit before this PR.
- **Tests that read a row's text.** Seven tests found a row's text with `get_by_label`. The row's control now has the same name, so they now ask for the `Label` node (`get_by_role_and_label(Role::Label, ..)`). In `wire_page_tests`, a click on the row label opened the named combo, so a small `show_row` helper scrolls the label into view instead. No assertion changes.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1119-op-page-names.md`.

Nothing visible changes.

## Pinning tests

- `egui_app::tests::op_page_names::every_operation_page_tab_names_every_input` (new). It walks every kind of the registry and every tab that the kind has, as `every_registry_kind_gets_its_tab_bar` does. It fails on an input with no name, or with one label named twice. Each failure line names the kind, the tab, the role and the row text. The walk reached more than 500 inputs.
  - On the 2D branch (before this commit), it is red with 667 lines. These are the header combos on each kind (Tool 205, Source 205, Coolant 202), Spindle speed (48), and the rest. On `main`, 5 more fields are red, which #4221 and #4218 fix.

title: fix(sim): the envelope vertical-rapid sweep keeps the lift-out-of-the-kerf rule
body:
Main is red since `d94c65fcf`: the step `motion suites: finish3d_hop_height` fails. This PR fixes the cause in `camcraft-sim` and does not change a test assertion.

## Cause

The fault is not an interaction of two merges. PR #4108 (#4062, merge `7b2587e15`) causes it alone. The post-merge run on `7b2587e15` (run 45871450597) already shows this failure. That run ended after the run on `d94c65fcf`, so the issue names `d94c65fcf` (#4198, which does not touch this code) as the first red commit. The run on the parent `26c626bb3` does not have this failure.

#4108 adds a finished-part sweep of the vertical rapids for `Mode::Envelope` paths (`vertical_rapid_hits` in `crates/sim/src/verify/solid.rs`). This sweep judges the whole cutter at the start pose of each vertical rapid. A 3D finish pass ends with the ball on the model. The finish law permits a contact up to the finish tolerance there. The retract up from that pose then starts "in the part", and the verifier gives `RapidInPart`. The quick gate of #4108 did not run the motion suite, because the diff touched only `sim` and `app`.

Readings on `origin/main` (`1c0152c91`):

- `a_retract_above_the_part_hops_clean`: `[RapidInPart { at: 368 }, RapidInPart { at: 394 }]`. Move 367 is a Feed that ends at `(12.113734, -14.31511, 8.904555)`. Move 368 is a vertical Rapid from that point up to z 25.
- `a_retract_below_the_high_run_never_takes_the_tool_into_the_part`: `[RapidInPart { at: 361 }, RapidInPart { at: 387 }]`, the same retracts.
- `inside_first_on_a_convex_part_with_a_low_retract_never_digs_in`: `RapidInPart { at: 349 }`. Move 348 is a Feed that ends at `(4.0, -6.317902, 8.904555)` on the mesa side. Move 349 goes straight up from there to z 25.

Each flagged move is an upward retract out of the end pose of a finish cut. The hops are correct. The finding is false.

## Fix

`judged()` in `crates/sim/src/verify/solid.rs` already has a rule for this case (`stack_hits`, the Area and Boundary reading). An upward vertical rapid that starts where a cut ended is judged like this:

- the shank and the holder are swept over the full rapid;
- the cutting edge is judged by the column that it rises into above its own top, at its largest radius;
- the start pose stays with the law of the cut.

The envelope sweep now uses the same rule (`stack_only || ex.vertical_rapids_only`). The #4062 fault stays refused: a retract through a roof hits the rise column. `thin_disc_retract_hits_canopy` and `dovetail_retract_hits_canopy` start at the end of a Feed, and they still give `RapidInPart { at: 1 }`. Descents and rapids that do not start at a cut keep the full sweep.

Decision: `docs/decisions/4211-envelope-lift-from-cut.md`.

## Tests

- `camcraft-motion --test finish3d_hop_height`: 5 passed (3 red before the fix).
- `camcraft-sim --test vertical_rapid_part`: 7 passed. The new pin `a_retract_from_a_finish_touch_on_the_wall_stays_clear` fails without the fix (`RapidInPart { at: 1 }`) and passes with it. It is added to the existing #4062 suite.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick`) on head `374e538c6`, on Windows: 11 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. The steps are the `camcraft-sim` lib, `mark_retract`, `midmove_pose`, `vertical_rapid_part`, `camcraft-motion` `solid_law`, and `camcraft-app` `probe_reach`, `real_tip_contour`, `thread_mill_rim`, `tool_body_drill_probe`.
- Strict clippy on `camcraft-sim` and `camcraft-motion` (`--all-targets`): clean.
- The `example_catalog*` suites did not run. No toolpath or post changes, so the catalog output does not change.

## Not exercised

- The light lane: the change touches no heavy test.
- No toolpath changes. The change only removes a false refusal of the verifier, so no posted G-code changes for a program that posted before.

Changelog: Fix: a 3D finish pass that ends on a wall no longer has its retract refused as a rapid in the part (a false finding since #4062).

Effort: low (fix in one function of `camcraft-sim`)

title: fix(rest): simulate the program ahead in the generation job, not at staging
body:
## What changed

A rest operation no longer simulates the program ahead while it is staged. The staging runs on the session thread (MCP) or the UI thread (GUI). The simulation now runs in the generation job, on the worker thread.

- `rest::prior_state` is split in two halves.
- `rest::stage_prior` does all world reads: the chain of operations ahead, the digest and the stock grid. It keeps the order and the refusals of before.
- `StagedPrior::simulate` cuts the cached moves ahead into the stock. It reads no world.
- `collect_job` keeps the staged half in the new field `GenJob::prior_staged`.
- `run_job` calls `GenJob::settle_prior` first. Thus the simulation runs on the job thread.
- The corner-relief reader (`zones_for_op`) settles the grid before its WCS yaw turn reads it.
- `prior_state` keeps its signature. It calls the two halves in sequence.

This covers 3D Pocket, Multi-Axis Rough, and a 2D Pocket or 2D Adaptive whose rest reads the previous operations.

## Cause

PR #3860 moved the generator of an MCP `generate` to a worker thread. But `StagedGeneration::new` calls `collect_job` on the session thread. For a rest operation, `collect_job` called `rest::prior_state`, which simulated all operations ahead. On a large part, this blocked every other MCP call for that time. The issue comment of 2026-11-24 names this open part.

## Tests

- Pin: `generate_staged::a_rest_reading_pocket_simulates_the_program_ahead_in_its_job_not_at_staging`.
  - It stages a 3D Pocket after a Face cut. It asserts that the staging thread simulates nothing.
  - It finishes the job on a second thread and asserts one simulation there.
  - It asserts that the path is equal to the path of the one-shot `GenerateOperation`.
- Red before the fix: `assertion left == right failed: staging simulates nothing; left: 1, right: 0`.
- Mutation: the simulation put back inside `stage` (the old timing) makes the pin red with the same message. With the fix restored, the pin is green.
- Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: green, 181 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (25.4 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Example catalog suites `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`: 46 passed, 0 failed (4 ignored by their own markers).
- Light lane `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: 6 steps, 0 failed.

## Goldens moved

None. The change moves where the simulation runs, not what it computes. The example catalog suites ran green, and `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" examples/catalog` is empty.

## Not exercised

- The original QA mould core project is not on this machine. I did not measure the time on it.
- A carried chain across setups (#318) stays eager on the staging thread. Its body comes from a per-thread cache. `docs/decisions/3035-rest-staging-worker.md` gives the reason.
- The stock grid is still built at staging (`first_held` needs the world). It is an allocation, not a simulation.
- Heavy lanes: not run. This is a `P3` PR (AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review").
- No UI change, so no screenshots.

## Open on #3035

- The run time of the generators on the mould core.
- A cancel point inside the generators.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `crates/app/src/operation/job.rs` or `crates/app/src/rest.rs`.

title: fix(adaptive): read the bore's star cell through offset rounding noise
body:
## What changed

- `adaptive::star::Star::new` cleans each opened row loop before the star laws read it. The new function `denoised` drops a vertex that is less than 1e-5 mm from the last vertex kept.
- The bore pin `BORE_PIN` in `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs` moves to `(1642, 1614, 300)`. The old pin stays as `BORE_PIN_BEFORE_4010`, and each platform pin test rejects it. The unmeasured-platform band is centred on the new pin with the same half-widths.
- New fixture: `crates/motion/tests/fixtures/bore_z15_center.txt`. It holds the Z 15 center area of the user's bore (328 vertices), recorded from the 3-D ladder.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/4010-bore-level-plan.md`.

## Cause

The Z 15 and Z 5 levels give the planner a 328-vertex disc outline. The opening of this outline at R2.5 keeps 20 edges that are 1 or 2 Clipper units long (1.4e-6 to 2.2e-6 mm). Integer rounding turns each of these edges back about the pole.

- `radial` reads such an edge as a shadow.
- `disc_in_kernel` reads the line of the edge as a wall through the area.

So the star cell was refused and the growth rings planned the disc. The 128-vertex outline of Z 10 and Z 0 has no such edges, so those levels kept the morph spiral. A probe in the planner showed this on each level:

- 328 points: row 0 fails, so the growth rings plan it (`Grown::Done`).
- 128 points: a star cell, so the morph spiral plans it.

## Readings (macOS arm64, release)

| Level | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Z 15, Z 5 | 1933 planar feeds, 918 arcs, 999.92 mm | 410 planar feeds, 78 arcs, 330.07 mm |
| Z 10, Z 0 | 397 planar feeds, 72 arcs, 334.31 mm | no change |
| Whole path | (4688, 4660, 1980) | (1642, 1614, 300) |

Z 15 and Z 5 now reach the wall at y -7.498 (before: 0.153 mm short in -Y). The path verifies clean with no fallback and no budget note. On unchanged upstream main `498382c8e`, macOS read `(4688, 4660, 1980)`. This is the same triple that Windows and Linux read.

## Tests

- Pins (in `camcraft-motion` lib, `machining2d::adaptive::tests`):
  - `the_users_z15_bore_is_one_star_cell`
  - `the_users_z15_bore_plans_the_short_spiral` (the walk is less than 500 mm, it does not cross itself, and the rest is under `HSM_REST_MAX`)
- Red before the fix: yes. Both failed on unchanged code with "the bore's walk is 1146.46 mm". The note was the same plan-B corner note, at (5.30, -5.30).
- Mutation: I put back `star.rs` from `upstream/main`, and the two pins went red. I restored the fix, and the two pins went green.
- `pocket3d_hsm` in release with `--include-ignored`: the bore test and all the pin and band tests pass. `the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level` fails at its `known-fail #1950` assert line, as it did before.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base 498382c8e`: 172 steps, 0 failed. This includes `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base 498382c8e`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. The example catalog suites ran green in the quick gate, and no `*.nc`, `*.cl` or catalog file changed. Only the count pin of `pocket3d_hsm` changed, as given above.

## Not exercised

- Windows x86_64 and Linux x86_64 are not measured after the fix. Before the fix they read the same triple as macOS, so the pin follows the macOS reading. Their next run confirms it or adds a platform triple.

title: fix(post): refuse a preset above the machine's last preset row
body:
Stacked on #4164 (merge #4164 first).

## What changed

- A machine file can state a new optional key, `controller.work_offset_max`. It is the highest work offset that the control holds. On a Heidenhain control it is the last row of the preset table.
- The machine reader and the raw post engine refuse a value that is not a whole number from 1 to 255. The message names the key.
- The key is an installation fact, the same as `tooling.max_tool_number` (#4164). The mirror carries it.
- The post engine refuses a `PARAM WorkOffset` above the key. The refusal names the setup and the key. It comes before any script hook runs, so it applies to each post.
- `fehlmann-picomax55.mch` states `"work_offset_max": 5`. Its description tells the shop to check the preset table at the control.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the key.
- A machine without the key keeps the post's own limit. A key above the post's own limit does not raise that limit.

## Cause

- Both Heidenhain posts accept presets 1..6 (`workOffsetMax = 6`).
- The Picomax preset table on the 2008 delivery CD (`PRESET.PR`) has rows 0..5 only (`docs/research/heidenhain/picomax-55-review.md`, defect 14).
- `Q339=+6` names a row that does not exist. The control stops with an alarm.
- The machine file had no place to state the row count.

The refusal is a hard error, not a counted warning. A counted warning was not enough: the Klartext post throws "missing or unsupported preset (WorkOffset)" when the engine holds back the offset, and that error hid the warning.

## Tests

Pins, in the `heidenhain_cycles` directory suite (new submodule `heidenhain_cycles/preset_rows.rs`, no new test binary):

- `preset_rows::heidenhain_posts_refuse_a_preset_above_the_machine_preset_table`: preset 5 posts with no warning, and preset 6 is refused with `setup Setup1: uses work offset 6` and `controller.work_offset_max`. It runs both posts on the raw file and on the parsed mirror.
- `preset_rows::an_unstated_or_larger_machine_maximum_keeps_the_post_limit`: no machine posts preset 6; a key of 99 posts preset 6 and refuses 7 with "work offsets 1-6 only".
- `preset_rows::a_malformed_work_offset_max_is_refused_by_name`: 0, -1, 2.5, "5" and 256 are refused by the reader and by the raw engine.

Red before the fix: yes. On the unchanged code the test did not compile (no `Machine::work_offset_max`). With the two field assertions taken out, all three tests failed: preset 6 posted, and no value was refused.

Mutations (each one red, then restored and green):

- Engine guard disabled: `heidenhain_posts_refuse_a_preset_above_the_machine_preset_table` red.
- Mirror line disabled: the same test red (mirrored input).
- Reader range widened to 256: `a_malformed_work_offset_max_is_refused_by_name` red.

Gate on the final head:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on `9d6ebbd62`: 343 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (29.3 min). The plan included each app suite that reads `heidenhain.cps`, `klartext_builtin`, `machine_controller` and the example catalog suites.
