title: feat(tools): document component table and undoable assembly commands
body:
## What changed

The document now holds shared tool components, and each tool can hold a component stack. A change to one shared component updates each tool that uses it, in one undo step.

- `crates/app/src/schema.rs`: two new schema components.
  - `DocumentComponents` is a world singleton. It has one row (`DocumentComponent`) for each component id. A row keeps the #3642 `ToolComponent` and the #3643 `ComponentGeometry` together.
  - `ToolAssembly` sits on a tool entity. It is the stack: for each node, a component id and its `Mount`.
- `crates/app/src/tool_assembly.rs`: reads and writes the table and the stacks, lists the users of a component (`users_of`), and derives a tool (`derive`) with the #3643 resolver.
- `crates/app/src/commands/tool_assembly.rs`: four undoable commands (below).
- `ChangeTool::assembled`: every `ChangeTool` law, with the body law judged against the body that lands in the same step.
- `DeleteTool` keeps the stack and restores it on undo. It moved to `commands/tool_delete.rs`, so that `commands/tool.rs` stays under 400 lines.
- Review fix 1: the generic `DeleteEntity` (the tree's delete) also restores the stack on undo. The two delete paths now snapshot and land one shared list, `ToolRecords` (`commands/tool_delete.rs`): the record, the number, the body, the cutter and the stack. A search found no other path that deletes a tool and restores it (the tool import's replace mode uses `DeleteTool`).
- The project loader clears the table, so that no row of the previous document leaks into the next one.
- Review fix 2: `NewDocument` (`crates/ui/src/state.rs`) clears the table too, next to the units, machine and post resets.
- `camcraft_app` re-exports `component`, `component_geometry` and `connection_code` of `camcraft_tools`, so that a caller outside `app` can make a table row. This adds no crate dependency.

## The commands and their refusals

| Command | Does | Refuses by name |
|---|---|---|
| `UpsertDocumentComponent` | Adds a row. A held id goes through `EditDocumentComponent`. | Each edit refusal, for a held id. |
| `EditDocumentComponent` | Replaces a row. Derives each tool that uses it again. Lands the table, each `ToolDef` and each `ToolBody` in one undo step. | An id that the document does not hold; an edit equal to the row; each `derive` or `ChangeTool` refusal of any user tool, with the component id and the tool name. Nothing changes. |
| `DeleteDocumentComponent` | Deletes an unused row. | An unknown id; a used component (names the tools). |
| `SetToolAssembly` (`new`, `clear`) | Sets a stack and lands the derived records in one undo step. `clear` removes the stack and keeps the records. | No such tool; an unknown component id; each #3642 fit and #3643 resolver refusal; a body in the flutes; each `ChangeTool` law; a lathe-held tool. |

Operations go Stale by their stamps: the tool record and `tool_body::digest` are in each stamp. No command writes a status.

## Readings

- An insert edit from `CCMT09T304` to `CCMT09T308` changes the corner radius of the Ø25 and the Ø32 cutters from 0.4 mm to 0.8 mm. The diameters stay 25 mm and 32 mm. The two Face operations go Stale.
- A `DCMT11T304` in the CC seats is refused: `the edit of tool component 'insert-cc' is refused: tool 'Fly25': assembly: ... does not fit ...`.

## Pinning tests

In `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders/assembly_cmds.rs` (joins the `tool_library_holders` suite):

- `one_shared_insert_edit_updates_two_assemblies_in_one_undo_step`
- `an_edit_one_assembly_cannot_take_is_refused_whole_by_name`
- `a_used_component_is_not_deleted_and_an_unused_one_is`
- `an_incompatible_stack_is_refused_by_name_and_changes_nothing`
- `set_tool_assembly_lands_the_derived_tool_and_body_in_one_undo_step`
- `a_deleted_tool_comes_back_with_its_stack`
- `review_generic_delete_undo_keeps_assembly` (review fix 1: delete through `DeleteEntity`, undo, the stack is back, and a shared edit updates the tool again)

In `crates/ui/tests/machine.rs` (next to `new_document_retires_the_machine_with_the_rest`):

- `new_document_clears_the_component_table` (review fix 2)

The two review pins fail on `7ce62c040` and pass on the new head.

## Not exercised

- The turning insert of the issue. The resolver has only the spindle side (#3643 is open for the lathe side). The tests use a milling insert in two indexable cutters. `derive` refuses a lathe-held tool by name.
- A solid cutting item through the commands. The resolver pins of #3643 cover it, and `derive` uses the solid tool's own record.

## What is left

- #3645: the table and the stacks in `.camproj` and `.camtools`, the user library, `library_ref`. Today the derived `ToolDef` and the drawn body save; the stack and the table do not.
- #3647: the MCP tools for the four commands (`MCP: <command>` follow-up). This PR adds no MCP tool.
- #3648: the UI. It also decides how a hand edit (`ChangeTool`, `SetToolBody`) and a stack live together. Today the next component edit derives the records again.
- #3646: the full `Tool` record of a multi-seat cutter. Today an insert gives the diameter and the corner radius only.

Decision: `docs/decisions/3644-component-commands.md`.

title: fix(pocket3d): start and exit picks for 3D Pocket
body:
## What changed

This is slice 3 of #3329: the 3D Pocket only. The 3D Pocket now takes a start point and an exit point. Its capability is the existing `PickCapability::Region` (the descent place of the first pass, and the end of the last pass). The picks seat the passes that the strategy already planned on each level. They never re-order the passes.

- Motion: `crates/motion/src/machining3d/level_seam.rs` (the seat laws and the refusals), `level_columns.rs` (the exact column law), `picked.rs` (`pocket3d_picked`, the plain or offset-shell ladder with "Do not touch" items, seated). The ladder gets one `picks` argument; each old caller passes `None`.
- `ladder.rs` gets smaller (441 lines, was 444): `mask_center` moves to `rest.rs`, unchanged.
- App: `OpType::Pocket3D => PickCapability::Region`; the 3D Pocket arm of `generate` calls `pocket3d_picked` only when a pick is set; `pick_kinds` refuses a pick under Adaptive and with Rest roughing; the MCP `edit_operation` schema names the region kind.

The title uses `fix`, because the issue has the `bug` label.

### Behaviour

- **Start:** on each level, the first ring of the first pass starts at its point nearest the start point. It cuts its whole lap back to that point. Then it runs on along its own cut, in its own direction, to its old start. From there the level is the automatic path, move for move: no link changes.
- **Start on zigzag rows:** an open row chain starts at its end nearest the start point (the chain runs the other way). Rows cut both ways, so the reversed chain cuts the same mix.
- **Exit:** on each level, the last ring of the last pass laps from its own start as before. Then it runs on along its own cut to its point nearest the exit point. An open zigzag chain ends at its end nearest the exit point. The operation's exit is the end of the last pass of the last level that cuts.
- **A level of one ring with the two picks:** the lap from the start point runs on straight to the exit point.
- A run-on re-traces a cut at the same depth. It removes no new material.
- The descent at the new start goes through the ladder's own entry rule (helix, ramp, arc, plunge and their stand-ins).
- The ladder reads the X and Y of a pick. A pick with a Z gets one note (`PICK_Z_UNREAD`).
- A ring of a ring strategy is never reversed (climb would become conventional cutting). The passes are never re-ordered (the ring order is the engagement law).
- With no pick, the output is the automatic path, byte for byte.

### Refusals (by name, never moved)

- A start point farther than 1.5 tool diameters from the start of the first pass of a level: `start point (x, y): the first pass of the 3D Pocket at Z z starts at (...), d mm from it, farther than the L mm ...`.
- A descent that the entry rule puts farther than that reach from the start point: `start point (x, y): the entry rule at Z z finds no room for its motion at the start point and descends at (...)`.
- An exit point farther than that reach from the end of the operation: `exit point (x, y): the last pass of the 3D Pocket at Z z ends at (...)`.
- A pick on a level that the Adaptive (HSM) plan spirals (its own entry bore and proved arcs).
- In the application, at the edit: a pick under the Adaptive strategy, and a pick with Rest roughing on.
- A plunge or retract column at a point that a pick moved that comes within the tool radius (less 0.01 mm) of the part.
  - The check is exact: each facet is clipped to the half-space above the column's foot, then `stock_sim::dist_seg_tri` measures the distance from the column's axis segment to what is left. There is no sampling. A distance that is not a number is a hit.
  - The moved points: the new start of a re-seated ring, the new end of a run-on, both ends of a reversed chain, and the descent place that the entry rule chose.
  - The islands law of the ladder already keeps each ring point clear above its level, so no ladder fixture reaches this refusal. It is a second, independent check, pinned by a unit test.

### Same-region rule

The start and the exit act on different passes of a level: the first pass and the last pass. Where a level has one pass, the two picks act on one ring: the lap from the start point runs on to the exit point (a re-trace, simple and safe). Where that one pass is an open chain, the exit is not moved: the exit reach law then refuses an exit that the chain does not end near.

### Mutation table

Each mutation was applied alone, then `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib level_seam` and `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test pocket3d_pass_start picks` ran (M11: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test start_exit_shared pocket3d`).

| # | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | No column law (`columns` checks no point) | RED: `the_column_law_is_exact_above_the_foot` |
| M2 | Column law tests only the two ends of the column (no segment distance) | RED: `the_column_law_is_exact_above_the_foot` |
| M3 | No start reach law | RED: `a_start_beyond_the_first_pass_is_refused_with_its_level`, `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M4 | No exit reach law | RED: `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M5 | No descent law | RED: `a_descent_far_from_the_start_point_is_refused`, `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M6 | No one-ring run-on from the start to the exit | RED: `a_level_of_one_ring_laps_from_the_start_and_runs_on_to_the_exit` |
| M7 | No run back to the old start after the re-seat | RED: `a_chain_keeps_its_links_and_moves_only_its_ends` |
| M8 | No exit run-on | RED: `a_chain_keeps_its_links_and_moves_only_its_ends`, `an_exit_pick_ends_the_operation_on_the_last_ring` |
| M9 | No zigzag reversal | RED: `zigzag_rows_start_at_their_end_nearest_the_start_point`, `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M10 | No refusal of an HSM level | RED: `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M11 | No application refusal (Adaptive, Rest roughing) | RED: `pocket3d_refuses_an_impossible_pick_by_name` |

## Readings

- Motion fixture (40 mm square pocket, 10 mm island, tool radius 3, Waterline, plunge entry, Z 8 / 3 / 0): a start at (30, 33) gives the descent of each level at (30, 32.2); the automatic descent is at (32.2, 32.2). An exit at (20, 11) gives the last cut end at (20, 12, 0), and the rise is straight up.
- Zigzag, 39.62 mm pocket, no island: a start at (38, 38) reverses the row chain; each level descends within 1 mm of (36.61, 36.61) (automatic: near (3.01, 3.01)).
- App brick (10 mm block in 40 x 40 stock, `EM-0600-4FL`, Offset rings, Z 6 / 2): a start at (-14, 10) gives each descent at (-12.961, 11.095) (automatic: (-12.636, 11.502)). An exit at (10, -21) gives the last cut end at (10, -19.99, 2).
- Reach with the 6 mm mill: 9 mm.

## Pinning tests

`camcraft-motion`, `tests/pocket3d_pass_start.rs`, new module `pocket3d_pass_start/picks.rs` (joins the existing suite, no new test binary):
- `no_pick_is_the_automatic_ladder_byte_for_byte` (Waterline, Offset rings, Zigzag, Auto; plain and offset shell)
- `a_start_pick_seats_the_first_ring_of_every_level` (also: the unread Z is said once)
- `an_exit_pick_ends_the_operation_on_the_last_ring` (exit alone, and start with exit)
- `zigzag_rows_start_at_their_end_nearest_the_start_point`
- `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` (start, exit, descent, HSM level)

Each picked path is gouge-checked at every cut move, sampled each 0.25 mm along its length (the island, the footprint, the floor). Each also cuts all that the automatic path cuts, level by level (a 0.5 mm grid of the swept tool disc).

`camcraft-motion` lib, `machining3d/level_seam_tests.rs`:
- `the_column_law_is_exact_above_the_foot`
- `a_level_of_one_ring_laps_from_the_start_and_runs_on_to_the_exit`
- `a_chain_keeps_its_links_and_moves_only_its_ends`
- `a_start_beyond_the_first_pass_is_refused_with_its_level`
- `a_descent_far_from_the_start_point_is_refused`

`camcraft-app`, `tests/start_exit_shared.rs`, new module `start_exit_shared/pocket3d.rs`:
- `pocket3d_starts_at_the_picked_point_and_ends_at_the_picked_exit` (also: no pick gives the automatic path again; gouge pin each 0.25 mm)
- `pocket3d_refuses_an_impossible_pick_by_name` (generation, and MCP edits under Adaptive and Rest roughing)
- `pocket3d_picks_ride_edit_operation_and_undo_restores_them` (MCP `edit_operation`, `get_job`, undo, redo, the schema text)
- Updated: `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` (3D Pocket is `Region`), `a_pick_on_a_kind_that_does_not_take_it_names_the_kind_and_the_reason` (Trace replaces 3D Pocket as the example of a kind that takes no pick).

## Goldens moved

## Not exercised

body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

Sub-PR 1 of 2 for #4176 (K2, the guide stage). This PR adds the ring and the row guide planners: the two families that 2D Pocket needs. Part 2 (the medial line, the trace of a chain and the helix) follows on the same issue.

## What changed

Public surface in `camcraft_pathkernel::guide`:
- `RingPlanner`: rings as level sets of the distance to the walls (Held 1991), spaced by the stepover of the choice. `RingRef::Boundary` uses all edges. `RingRef::Part` uses the part walls only; its rings are open at the stock edge.
- Clean-up rings fill the area that the regular rings leave. The 0.1 mm2 guard makes the result `Incomplete` with each gap named.
- `RowPlanner`: rows at the angle, spaced evenly at the stepover or less, clipped to the cutter-centre area. A closing ring is added on request.
- `Guides`: sends rings and rows to their planners. It refuses the medial line and the trace with `FAMILY_NOT_YET` until part 2 (law 4).
- `Mark`, `MarkKind` (`FullWidth`, `Fill`, `Closing`; `#[non_exhaustive]`), `Span`. `GuideSet::with_marks` and `GuideSet::marks`. `GuideSet::new` does not change.
- `FullWidth` names each stretch where the tool disc overlaps no disc of the next deeper curves and no air (#3788). K3 and K4 read it.
- Named refusals: `NOT_RINGS`, `NOT_ROWS`, `CIRCLE_NOT_YET`, `BAND_NOT_YET`, `OFFSET_BELOW_CENTER`, `WALL_STRIP_UNCUT`, `NO_RING`, `TOO_MANY_RINGS`, `TOO_MANY_ROWS`, `STEP_ABOVE_DIAMETER`, `BAD_TOL`, `NOT_PLANAR`, `GUIDE_GEOMETRY`, `BAD_STRETCH`, `MARK_NO_CURVE`, `MARK_OFF_CURVE`.

The kernel crate still depends on `camcraft-geometry` only. No geometry function was added. No old planner and no golden changes: with the default switch the output is identical.

## Pins

- `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/guide_rings.rs` (11 tests): level-set spacing, law 1 under a permuted selection, Part equal to Boundary without a stock edge, the waist (two lobes, a neck narrower than two steps: the full-width stretch of each strand is named), clean-up rings, a small piece kept (0.01 mm2), a ring count, rings round a part, each refusal, `Guides`.
- `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/guide_rows.rs` (6 tests): row spacing, rows at an angle with a closing ring, gaps named without a closing ring, law 1, refusals, mark checks. Helpers in `guide_kit.rs`.
- `crates/motion/tests/pass_start_levels/kernel_rings.rs`: the kernel rings against the recorded old rings (#3750 goldens). Readings (agreement within 0.02 mm):
  - Dog bone, 2D Offset round the part: each point of the 29 kernel rings is on each of the 7 old plans with a known stock. Named difference: the old plan also walks the stock outline; the kernel does not, because the outline is air (#4025 decision 4).
  - `auto_blind` is not compared: an Outside kernel region needs the stock.
  - The band round the disc: the 2D Pocket rings and the 3-D level rings are the old Auto rings, both ways. Named difference: the old Inside and Outside plans build their own pieces for each start side (#3316, #3750).
- Law suite registry: this PR adds no registry row. When 2D Pocket moves, its row in `tests/laws/registry.rs` becomes `State::Moved` with `Planners { guide: Box::new(Guides), .. }`.

title: fix(post): refuse a tool number above the machine tool table
body:
## What changed

- The machine file can state a new optional key, `tooling.max_tool_number`. It is the highest tool number that the control's tool table holds.
- The machine reader and the raw post engine refuse a value that is not a whole number of 1 or more. The message names the key.
- The key is an installation fact, the same as `tooling.tool_change`. The mirror carries it. Scripts read it as `machine.toolNumberMax`.
- `fehlmann-picomax55.mch` states `"max_tool_number": 254`.
- `heidenhain-klartext.cps` refuses a higher tool number with a script error.
- `heidenhain.cps` refuses a higher tool number with a counted warning. It refuses a spindle speed above the machine maximum in the same way.
- A machine without the key keeps the old behaviour. Klartext keeps its limit of 32767. DIN/ISO has no limit.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/4087-tool-table-max.md`.

## Cause

The Picomax tool table has 254 lines (MP 7260 = 254, and the programming manual p. 2-16). No machine fact carried this limit. The Klartext post accepted tool numbers up to 32767, and the DIN/ISO post accepted all tool numbers. A program with tool 255 posted, and then the control stopped it with an alarm.

`tooling.number_of_tools` is a different fact. It counts the distinct tools in a changer (`check_tool_count`). It does not limit the tool number.

## Tests

Review fix head: `576ae80811ca4b404a6260eafed39472df348b27`.

| Revert only the test fix while keeping that error probe | Green: confirms the old test accepted the error |
| Restore the test; throw the same error only in `heidenhain-klartext.cps` | Red: tool 254 must post; 1 failed |

All probes were removed. No production file changed in this review fix.

The quick gate passed 1,227 post tests and 1,707 app tests. It left 42 app tests ignored as declared.

The catalog and golden suites ran in full:

body:
## What changed

Dovetail cutters (`ToolKind::Dovetail`) now read `corner_r` across geometry, verification, stock simulation, and the UI:

- `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs`: `Head::Dove` stores `{ cot, corner_r }`. `Undercut::rho` evaluates the corner arc up to `s_tan = c * (1 + sin t)` and the tangent flank above `s_tan`. `Undercut::contact()` returns `(r, corner_r)`.
- `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs`: `undercut::refusal` checks `corner_r` in `[0, diameter / 2]`, `s_tan <= flute_len + NECK_MEETS`, and neck clearance against the rounded flank.
- `crates/tools/src/undercut.rs` and `crates/tools/src/meridian.rs`: `head_outline` and `Tool::meridian` emit the rounded corner arc and straight flank.
- `crates/sim/src/verify/`: `Cutter::atoms` emits `Prof::Zone` (`[0, s_tan]`) and `Prof::Dove` (`[s_tan, flute_len]`), or one `Prof::Zone` when the flank top meets `s_tan`. `swept::rho_expanded` and `rotary_geom::shapes` handle `Prof::Zone`. `Frame` moves to `probe_frame.rs` under the 400-line rule.

title: feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour
body:
feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour

Wire Contour gains the three polish cuts of #3216. Each is stated, never
inferred, and refused by name where it has nothing to state.

What changed

- Closing overlap (closed profiles). `WireContourOp.overlap` and
  `WireParams.overlap` (mm, default 0) ride the cut past the seam by the
  stated arc length before the lead-out returns to the threading point,
  so the start of the cut is burnt over and no witness mark is left.
  The past-seam extension walks the ring from the seam point and cuts
  the last point to the exact remainder; the kerf law judges the return
  move like every other. Refused: with tabs (tabs pin the seam), on an
  open run (no seam), at a negative or non-finite length. A skim
  inherits the overlap. The note says the ride.
- Centre-line slit (open runs). New `WireSide::Centre`: the wire rides
  the run itself, the kerf burns both sides, no side is kept - so the
  kerf law has no product to protect and is not applied, while the
  corner/doubling-back law and the run-out laws still refuse what the
  wire cannot follow. The note says "no side kept".
- Skims on open runs. `check_passes` no longer refuses an open run; the
  offset-ordering laws judge it like a closed profile. `wire_passes`
  routes each open-side skim through the open-run generator: every pass
  re-enters from the air at the run's start end, at its own run-in
  point, walked in the run's own direction - a reversed pass on an open
  run is refused by name (one pinned semantic), and no move joins one
  pass's run-out to the next pass's run-in (the wire is threaded anew).
- Wire verify (sim). `CutSide::Centre` is judged as an open run whose
  kerf law is skipped by statement (`CENTRE_SKIP` on the report line);
  the ends' clearance is still judged. Skims on an open run are
  generated but named as not verified here yet (the verify reads one
  open pass) - a follow-up can extend the open law to per-pass kerfs.
- App, file and UI. The overlap rides the seed, the command door's
  sanity, the op stamp (only when stated, so no existing stamp moves)
  and the project DTO (`overlap`, absent reads 0); `side` reads and
  writes `centre`. The wire page gains the Closing overlap row and the
  Centre choice; its test count grows by one.

Pinning tests

- `the_closing_overlap_rides_past_the_seam_and_is_refused_without_a_seam`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): ride length past the seam, inherited
  skim ride, lead-out home, and each refusal by name.
- `a_centre_slit_rides_the_run_itself_and_takes_skims_from_the_air`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): centre ride on the line, air threading
  per pass at its own offset, reversed refused.
- `skim_laws_refuse_by_name`: the open-run skim refusal is replaced by
  the offset laws accepting it.
- `wire_closing_overlap_and_centre_side_apply_and_undo` (camcraft-ui).

Readings: the overlap ride of 1.0 mm on a 40x20 die ends at
(1.000, -9.835) with K = 0.165; a centre slit's left skim threads at
(60.000, -1.145) against the rough's (60.000, -1.165).

Not exercised

- The Sodick post refuses an open run's skims by name at its rapid
  guard: its manual states no such pass structure, and the generic ISO
  post is the one that cuts, travels and threads anew around each
  boundary.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, 665 steps)

- All sim, motion, app and ui suites green, the three pinning tests
